page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at two threads per core. The processor features 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache, supporting vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 128.0 GB, yielding a high memory density ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or dedicated graphics accelerators, relying exclusively on remote network storage for persistent disk access. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps. Synthetic memory benchmarks show large-block uncached read speeds of 102.07 GB/sec and write speeds of 59.04 GB/sec, while in-memory throughput testing records 15.46 million Redis SET operations per second.

CPU performance remains consistent within average mid-tier ranges, scoring 9,464.0 points in Geekbench multi-core testing and 20,751.25 points in PassMark CPU evaluations. While smaller language model inference functions reliably, prompt processing on medium 7B models drops to 30.95 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators. Given the memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance functions effectively for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, including Redis caching tiers, large database buffer pools, and in-memory analytical pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from an 8-core Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, the instance maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive architectures. The hardware profile includes AVX-512 with VNNI and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions, paired with a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local storage or GPUs, requiring external storage volumes for stateful data retention. Benchmark testing places its computational and memory throughput within the median enterprise range, registering 15.46 million Redis SET operations per second and 102.07 GB/sec large-block memory read bandwidth. Due to its large memory capacity and dedicated compute allocation, the instance provides cost-effective density for memory-bound tasks such as in-memory databases, large Redis caches, memory-resident analytics, and enterprise backend applications.
